verses.text: Then the high priest asked Stephen, "Are these things true?"
Stephen answered, "Brothers and fathers, listen to me. The God of glory appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran.
God said to him, 'Leave your country and your relatives, and go to the land I will show you.'
So he left the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. After his father died, God sent him to this land where you now live.
God gave him no land here, not even enough to put his foot on. But even though Abraham had no child yet, God promised that he and his descendants after him would own this land.
God told him this: 'Your descendants will live as strangers in a land that is not theirs. They will be made slaves and treated badly for four hundred years.
But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves,' God said, 'and after that they will come out and worship me in this place.'

Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision. So when Abraham became the father of Isaac, he circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of the twelve fathers of our nation.
"Those fathers were jealous of Joseph, so they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him.
He rescued him from all his troubles. He gave Joseph wisdom and made Pharaoh, king of Egypt, like him. So Pharaoh made Joseph ruler over Egypt and over all his palace.
Then there was a famine in all of Egypt and Canaan, and people suffered greatly. Our ancestors could not find food.
When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for the first time.
On their second visit, Joseph told his brothers who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.
Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five people in all.
So Jacob went down to Egypt, and there he and our ancestors died.
Their bodies were brought back to Shechem and buried in the tomb Abraham had bought with silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
"As the time came near for God to keep his promise to Abraham, the number of our people in Egypt grew and grew.
Then a new king who knew nothing about Joseph came to rule Egypt.
He was cruel to our people and treated our ancestors badly. He forced them to leave their babies outside so that they would die.
At that time Moses was born, and he was a very beautiful child in God's eyes. For three months he was cared for in his father's house.
When he was put outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.
Moses was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in what he said and did.
"When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his own people, the people of Israel.
He saw one of them being treated badly by an Egyptian, so he went to help him. He struck the Egyptian and killed him to defend the man.
Moses thought his own people would understand that God was using him to save them, but they did not understand.
The next day Moses saw two of them fighting, and he tried to make peace between them. He said, 'Men, you are brothers. Why do you hurt each other?'
But the man who was hurting the other pushed Moses aside and said, 'Who made you our ruler and judge?
Do you want to kill me like you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'
When Moses heard this, he ran away to the land of Midian. He lived there as a foreigner and had two sons.
"After forty years, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
When Moses saw it, he was amazed. As he went closer to look, he heard the voice of the Lord:
'I am the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' Moses shook with fear and did not dare to look.
Then the Lord said to him, 'Take off your sandals, because the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have seen how badly my people are treated in Egypt. I have heard their groans, and I have come down to rescue them. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.'
"This is the same Moses the people had rejected when they said, 'Who made you our ruler and judge?' God sent him to be their ruler and rescuer, through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
He led them out of Egypt and did wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the desert for forty years.
This is the Moses who told the people of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people.'
He was with the people in the desert, with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our ancestors. He received living words from God to pass on to us.
"But our ancestors refused to obey him. They pushed him aside, and in their hearts they wanted to go back to Egypt.
They said to Aaron, 'Make us gods who will lead us. As for this Moses who brought us out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
That was when they made an idol shaped like a calf. They brought sacrifices to it and held a party to celebrate what they had made with their own hands.

But God turned away from them and let them worship the stars in the sky. This agrees with what is written in the book of the prophets: 'People of Israel, did you bring me animals to kill and sacrifices for forty years in the desert?
No, you carried the tent of the god Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, idols you made to worship. So I will send you away beyond Babylon.'
"Our ancestors had the tent of meeting with them in the desert. It was made just as God told Moses, following the pattern he had seen.

Later our ancestors who received the tent brought it with them when they went with Joshua into this land. They took the land from the nations God drove out ahead of them. The tent stayed here until the time of David.
David found favour with God and asked if he could build a house for the God of Jacob.
But it was Solomon who built the house for God.
"But the Most High does not live in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says,
'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me? says the Lord. Where is the place I will rest?
Did not my hand make all these things?'
"You stubborn people! Your hearts and ears are closed to God. You always fight against the Holy Spirit, just as your ancestors did.
Was there ever a prophet your ancestors did not attack? They even killed those who told ahead of time about the coming of the Righteous One. And now you have betrayed and murdered him.
You received the law that was given through angels, but you have not obeyed it."
When the members of the council heard this, they were furious and ground their teeth at him.
But Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit. He looked up to heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at God's right side.
He said, "Look! I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right side of God!"
Then they shouted loudly and covered their ears. They all rushed at him together,
dragged him out of the city, and began to throw stones at him. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
Then he fell on his knees and cried out, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." When he had said this, he fell asleep in death.
